---
title: "Evaluate Out-of-Sample Genomic Prediction"
---

## Evaluate Out-of-Sample Genomic Prediction {.unnumbered}


### Description

Computes prediction accuracy metrics for test individuals. Designed
to complement <code>predict.masreml()</code> for out-of-sample evaluation.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>evaluate_prediction(gebv, y, h2 = NULL, tbv = NULL, fitted_prob = NULL)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="gebv">gebv</code></td>
<td>
numeric vector of predicted GEBV for test individuals
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="y">y</code></td>
<td>
numeric vector of observed phenotypes for test individuals
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="h2">h2</code></td>
<td>
numeric, heritability from fitted model for r_MG computation.
Typically <code>fit\$varcomp\$h2</code> (single component) or a specific
component. If NULL, r_MG is returned as NA.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="tbv">tbv</code></td>
<td>
numeric vector of true breeding values (simulation only).
If provided, <code>r_MG_true = cor(gebv, tbv)</code> is computed directly
without requiring h2. If NULL, r_MG_true is NA.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="fitted_prob">fitted_prob</code></td>
<td>
numeric vector of fitted probabilities P(y=1) for
binary trait, typically <code>pred\$fitted</code> from <code>predict.masreml()</code>.
If NULL, AUC is returned as NA.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Value

data.frame with columns:


<ul>
<li> <code>r_test_y</code>: predictive ability. Continuous: <code>cor(gebv, y)</code>.
Binary: <code>cor(fitted_prob, y)</code> on the observed (probability) scale.

</li>
<li> <code>r_test_g</code>: <code>cor(gebv, tbv)</code> — accuracy vs true BV
on the genetic-value scale (uses <code>gebv</code> for both continuous
and binary). NA if <code>tbv</code> NULL.

</li>
<li> <code>bias</code>: regression slope. Continuous: <code>lm(y ~ gebv)</code>;
binary: <code>lm(y ~ fitted_prob)</code> = <em>calibration slope</em>.
Both interpret 1.0 = unbiased / well-calibrated, &lt;1 over-dispersion,
&gt;1 under-dispersion.

</li>
<li> <code>r_MG</code>: <code>cor(gebv, y) / sqrt(h2)</code> — heritability-adjusted
accuracy on the GEBV scale (uses <code>gebv</code> not <code>fitted_prob</code>
even for binary, so <code>h2</code> is on the same scale). NA if <code>h2</code>
NULL.

</li>
<li> <code>AUC</code>: area under ROC curve, computed from <code>fitted_prob</code>.
Rank-invariant so unaffected by inverse-link transformation. NA if
<code>fitted_prob</code> NULL.

</li>
<li> <code>RMSE</code>: continuous: <code>sqrt(mean((gebv - y)^2))</code>; binary:
<code>sqrt(mean((fitted_prob - y)^2))</code> $\approx$ <code>sqrt(Brier)</code>.

</li></ul>



### See Also

<code>predict.masreml</code>, <code>compute_accuracy</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masreml")

d   <- load_data("small")
y   <- d$pheno$y_cont_qtl_snp; names(y) <- d$pheno$id
fit <- masreml(y[d$train_idx],
               markers = list(snp_add = d$snp[d$train_idx, ]))
pred <- predict(fit,
  markers_new   = list(snp_add = d$snp[d$test_idx, ]),
  markers_train = list(snp_add = d$snp[d$train_idx, ]))

# Continuous trait — pass TBV for the standard breeding-value accuracy
tbv_te <- d$pheno$tbv_qtl_snp[d$test_idx]; names(tbv_te) <- names(pred$GEBV)
evaluate_prediction(
  gebv = pred$GEBV,
  y    = y[d$test_idx],
  h2   = fit$varcomp$h2["snp_add"],
  tbv  = tbv_te
)




```
